context: Reproduce framing on CRLF input; route the writer's CSV read through the same trailing-delimiter detection as ingest; fix regex asserts for Windows message variants.
description: Nightly Validation test (windows-latest, 3.10/3.12) fails 8+ tests in tests/unit/core/data_organization/test_sorting.py with pyarrow.lib.ArrowInvalid 'CSV parse error: Expected N columns, got N+1' on rows like '3|1998-03-01|' — the trailing-pipe framing class documented for dbgen EOL divergence (PR #1053 fixed the ingest path via get_data_extension; the sorted-parquet writer test path apparently still mis-frames on Windows CRLF/trailing-delimiter). Also two regex-assert failures in the same file (test_single_column_sorting_rejects_unknown_column, test_partition_column_validation). Pre-existing: fails at c0c96bddb (before agent-instruction PRs) and at 06484de94. Discovered 2026-07-29 during agent-instruction remediation close-out.

preserves.behavior: Existing green behavior on macOS/Linux fast lanes

verifications.expected: all pass; Windows proof via next Nightly Validation run

work_units.evidence: Root cause: _source_has_trailing_delimiter() probed the last 2 bytes for b'|\n'; a CRLF file's tail is b'|\r\n', so trailing-delimiter framing was misread as absent on Windows and PyArrow got N+1 fields for N column names. Replaced the private byte probe with the shared benchbox.utils.file_format.has_trailing_delimiter (already used by every other reader; reads text-mode so CRLF is normalized, and compares field counts rather than matching a byte tail). Proven across 4 framings (LF/CRLF x trailing/clean) - private probe was wrong only on CRLF+trailing; shared helper correct in all 4. Rung 1: 29 passed -n 0.
work_units.summary: Reproduce and fix the trailing-pipe/CRLF framing in the sorted-parquet writer test path

work_units.evidence: No regex change was needed - the unit's premise (cross-platform error-message drift) was a misdiagnosis. Proven: _read_tbl_files() runs before _sort_table(), so on CRLF input pyarrow raised ArrowInvalid ('CSV parse error: Expected 2 columns, got 3') before the ValueError could be raised. pytest.raises(ValueError, match=...) therefore failed on exception TYPE, not on message text; the messages are identical on all platforms. Both asserts pass once w1 fixes the framing probe. Added test_crlf_source_still_reports_unknown_sort_column to pin the validation-outranks-framing ordering, plus test_reads_trailing_delimiter_tbl_with_crlf_line_endings; both write explicit CRLF bytes so the Windows-only framing is now exercised on every platform. Verified non-vacuous: both fail with the exact nightly signature when the prod fix is reverted.
work_units.summary: Fix the two regex assertion failures for cross-platform error messages
